full_judgment:
By this Rule the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 were called upon to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 5-5-1996, passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Bhola in Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 1996 arising out of Title Suit No. 28 of 1994 directing the petitioners to furnish security bond within 7 days, should not be set aside. 

 2. Material facts for disposal of the Ruleare that the defendants in the original suit are the petitioners in this case. The opposite party Nos. 1 & 2 as plaintiffs instituted the Title Suit No. 28 of 1994 for declaration of their title in respect of the suit land described in 'Ka' schedule of the plaint and for further declaration that the decree in question as described in 'Kha' schedule of the plaint was fraudulent and not binding upon them. Thereafter, plaintiffs opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 on 22-2-1994 also filed an application under Order XXXIX rule 1 read with section 151 of the Code seeking for temporary injunction in respect of the suit land. The trial Court issued show cause notices upon the defendants-petitioners, along with it also granted ad-interim injunction restraining them from encroaching upon the suit land and disturbing the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs-opposite party Nos. 1 & 2. Thereafter, on 3-2-1996 the plaintiffs opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 1996 for violation of the order of injunction under Order XXXIX rule 2(3) of the Code against the defendants-petitioners with the allegation that the latter along with their lathials on 15-2-1995 had cut and taken away the standing crops from the suit land in violation of court's order and subsequently on 21-1-1996 they encroached upon the suit land and ploughed the same. The Plaintiffs-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 also by an application under section 94 of the Code have prayed for issuance of warrant upon the defendants- petitioners, and to direct them to furnish bond along with surety for their appearance before the court otherwise for detaining them in civil prison. It has been further alleged in the revisional application that by filing written objection on 23-4-1996 the defendants-petitioners have denied the material allegations of the plaintiffs-opposite parties application as being false, concocted, fictitious and ill motivated. The learned Assistant Judge upon hearing the parties passed the impugned order dated 15-5-1996 directing the petitioners to furnish security bond along with their appearance within 7 days, in default of which warrant of arrest would be issued against them. 

 4. Mr Farid Ahmed on behalf of Mr Swapan Kumar Mitra appearing for the petitioner submits that since the petitioners have sought punishment in (violation) Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 1996 filed under Order XXXIX rule 2(3) of the Code, the learned Assistant Judge was not legally authorised to pass the impugned order under section 94 of the Code. In support of his contention he has relied upon a decision held in the case of Mosharraf Hossain Mia vs Mosammat Hasina Begum and others reported in 43 DLR 254. 

 6. As for myself, I have been taken through the impugned order and other material on record. From the impugned order itself, it appears that the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 have brought a violation case against the petitioners under Order XXXIX rule 2(3) of the Code on the allegation of violation of the Court's order passed under Order XXXIX rule 1 of the Code. While the said proceeding was pending the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 have sought punishment upon the petitioners under section 94 of the Code on the same allegation of violation of the Court's order. In order to examine the legal propriety of the impugned order, let me quote the relevant provisions from section 94 which run as follows: 

 7. In the context of above provision of law, the learned Advocate for the petitioner took me to the case of Mosharraf Hossain Mia vs Mosammat Hasina Begum and others reported in 43 DLR 254. 

 8. In the said case the plaintiff brought a suit for declaration against certain kabalas relating to the suit land and in pursuance of an application for temporary injunction by the plaintiff, learned Subordinate Judge passed an order of status quo with respect to the possession of the suit land. The plaintiff then filed two violation cases against the defendants and while those cases were pending, the plaintiff by an application under section 94 of the Code sought arrest of the defendants and to furnish security bond on the allegation that the defendant in violations of court's order had gone to damage the suit properties. The learned Subordinate Judge allowed the prayer against which the defendants petitioners on an application under section 115(1) of the Code moved this Court and their Lordship's in the Division Bench, of this court after examining the legal provisions as contained in section 94 along with other allied provision laid down in section 2(16) of the Code, Order XXXVIII, rule 1, section 16( d) and section 151 of the Code, held the view that the impugned order of the learned Subordinate Judge is not sustainable in law. 

 9. The fact and circumstances of the instant case discussed above are almost similar to that of the case referred to above from the legal point of view. So, with respectful agreement with the view of their Lordships of the Division Bench, it may be held that when a violation case under Order XXXIX rule 2(3) of the Code is pending before a court, no application under section 94 of the Code lies seeking direction upon the same offender for furnishing security for their appearance in default to commit them in civil prison. In that view of the matter, the learned Assistant Judge appears to have committed error of law in his decision in passing the impugned order dated 5-5-1996 occasioning failure of justice and, as such the said order being not legally sustainable is liable to be set aside. 

 11. The impugned order passed by the learned Assistant Judge is set aside and he is directed to dispose of the (violation) Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 1996 as early as possible preferably within 6(six) months from the date of receipt of the order in accordance with law.
